concept: Receipt to blueprint to receipt: two hand-drawn receipts ask "am I overpaying?", one warm chalk pipeline grows step by step with real paper cut-outs, the creator's own two systems show where the price is earned, and the receipts return to pay off the hook.
palette: #14110F background: warm near-black for every panel and card
#FFF3DC chalk: main line work, labels, caption text
#FFD23F accent: numbers, the rupee sign, highlighter sweeps on paper cuts, MY READ tags
#FF8A3D Fable 5.2: its receipt, tag, lane and the lit vision slot
#6EC5FF Haiku 5.5: its receipt, tag and lane
#FF7EB6 Opus 5.5: lane and tag (kept neutral in the plate frame)
#7CE38B positive: ticks, RELEASED, 97% lower cost, the shrinking error bar
#FF6B5E caution, used small: the warning mark in M5 and Haiku's overshoot only, never as a wash
#8C857A warm grey: dashed 'my read' lines, NOT DISCLOSED chips, ghosted S4/S5, footnotes
#F6EBD2 paper cream: real page crops with a torn edge
typography: Section cards: huge condensed uppercase sans (Anton or Bebas style), chalk white with one word or number in yellow, filling about 80% of frame width. Diagram labels: hand-lettered marker face, upper-case for node names, minimum 44 px at 1440 wide; footnotes minimum 32 px in warm grey. Numbers: condensed bold, 2 to 3 times the label size, yellow; check the face has a rupee glyph. Paper cuts keep the PDF's own serif, never re-typed. Captions: one line, bold clean sans, chalk white with a dark stroke, sitting low in the creator half but above Instagram's bottom overlay (check against the safe-zone guide), max about 5 words per caption.
texture: 4 to 6 px chalk-marker lines with slight wobble and round caps, drawn on stroke by stroke. Solid line = disclosed, dashed warm-grey line = my read, used consistently from the legend onward. Warm near-black background with faint paper grain, no gradients, no 3D, no stock icons. Soft 8 to 12 px glow on accent strokes only. Paper cuts: cream page crops, scissor/torn edge, 2 degree tilt, soft shadow, yellow highlighter sweep at about 60% opacity. Creator footage: warm grade, lifted skin tones, 3 to 5% grain, applied in post so the same takes can be graded cold for the trial reel.
music: Upbeat, warm bed around 100 to 110 BPM: plucks or kalimba, soft kick, light bass, starting on the first receipt tick. Bass drops out and the bed thins on "the strange part" (curious, not dark), rebuilds through graded RL, one-second music-only breath for the effort dial, beat drop on the "wrapper" hold, brighter lift into the Meal Analyser section, bass accent on "It thinks", steady under the tips, receipt motif returns at the payoff, riser on the CTA that cuts to silence on the glimpse. Licensed or royalty-free, ducked about 18 dB under voice. No drone anywhere in this cut; that belongs to the trial reel.
sfx_palette: bass impact (section cards, wrapper beat drop, 'It thinks')
soft two-note 'uh-oh' tone, playful not alarming
pacing: About 90 to 91 s, a visual change roughly every 3 s. Fastest at the hook (three changes in 6.5 s) and the montage (about 1.6 s per clip); the paper section runs one step per 4.5 to 7 s as draw first, paper cut second; longest holds are the plate numbers (about 4 s) and the wrapper pull-back (about 2.5 s). Timing note: beats M1 to M5 follow the screenplay clock; from 29 s I re-estimated from word count because M6 carries 38 spoken words (about 13 s) in a 5 s slot and M7 has no spoken line. So M6 runs 29 to 42, the effort dial gets a 1 s music-only breath at 42, and M8 to M11 shift later (M11 loses its unspoken slack). M12 and M13 land back on the screenplay clock; the CTA plus glimpse ends near 90.8 s. All times are estimates to be conformed to the recorded audio; visuals land on or just before the word.
references: Chalk-talk explainer on a blackboard: white and bright marker lines on a dark surface, drawn live, one idea per frame
Documentary paper-collage inserts: a torn page excerpt sliding in with a single highlighter sweep
A long thermal till receipt unrolling off a counter next to a tiny one
Engineering blueprint pull-back: the whole system revealed at once after seeing its parts
Transit-map lanes: four coloured parallel lines, one per model, with stops as jobs
Sports-broadcast stat tags landing on a still image, used for the plate estimates
A hand-made checklist card with green ticks, the kind people screenshot

keyframes.emotion: Honest framing, I can trust this

keyframes.top_visual: S1 draws small at the left of the frame. S2 builds big: a teacher model holding a prompt card, an arrow to a student model with no prompt card, then an arrow into the training box. Label under the chain in grey: 'prompt distillation' (my label).
keyframes.motion: Chain draws node by node on the phrase; the prompt card drops away from the student.
keyframes.creator_direction: Finger count 'one' on 'First'.

keyframes.emotion: It's in the paper, not a guess
keyframes.top_visual: Cut P1 (p.131) slides in across the top panel; yellow highlighter sweeps over 'later added to Claude Mythos 5.2's training data' on 'ended up in its training data'. Cut P2 (p.11) tucks in small behind it. Dashed tag: MY READ (medium): fine-tune on model transcripts first, then RL. One-line grey footer for pausers: models now help train their successors.
keyframes.motion: Cut slides in with a 2 degree tilt; highlighter sweeps left to right in 0.4 s.
keyframes.transition_in: Paper slide over the dimmed diagram
keyframes.creator_direction: Glances up toward the cut as it lands, then back to lens.

keyframes.shot: Full-frame creator, tight punch-in (about 1.4x), face centred high.
keyframes.motion: Slow push-in during the line.
keyframes.music: Bass drops out, bed thins to plucks
keyframes.creator_direction: Lowers voice, small lean toward lens, one raised finger. Curious, not worried.

keyframes.top_visual: Side branch S2b grows off S2: a rubric card reading 'never flag the user's instructions' draws, then morphs into a clipboard with a small coral warning mark on 'trust anything pasted'.
keyframes.motion: Rubric card folds and redraws as the clipboard; warning mark pops last.
keyframes.sfx: Pencil run, soft two-note 'uh-oh' on the warning mark
keyframes.creator_direction: Two hands: left hand 'one rule', right hand 'turned into'.

keyframes.emotion: Nobody planned that, and they fixed it
keyframes.top_visual: Cut P3 (p.131) lands over the branch; highlighter on 'even though no part of our training incentivized this'. A green patch arrow loops from the clipboard back to the training box with small Cut P4 (p.133) labelled 'the fix'. Solid DISCLOSED stamp. Grey footer: training data generalises in ways nobody wrote down.
keyframes.motion: Highlighter sweep on the phrase; patch arrow loops in 0.5 s.
keyframes.music: Bass returns on the patch click
keyframes.creator_direction: Slow head shake on 'Nobody trained that', then a small nod as the patch lands.

keyframes.emotion: So that's how it gets good
keyframes.top_visual: S3 builds as the core of the pipeline: a task card, an arrow to a checker program box, then a reward arrow looping back into the model box. Dashed tag: MY READ (high): rewards are mostly machine-graded. Cut P5 (p.95) slides in small once the loop closes.
keyframes.motion: One node per phrase; the reward arrow keeps circulating slowly as a loop.
keyframes.transition_in: Diagram pans right to the next empty slot
keyframes.sfx: Pencil run, snip on the cut
keyframes.creator_direction: Hand on chest for 'My read', then three small beats in the air for task, grade, reinforce.

keyframes.shot: Bottom half punches in to 1.25x on the line.
keyframes.top_visual: A small model figure in S3 turns its head from the task card to stare at the checker box; the checker glows yellow, the task card dims.
keyframes.on_screen_text: STUDIES THE EXAMINER, NOT THE SUBJECT
keyframes.motion: Head turn in 0.3 s; text lands in two halves on the two phrases.
keyframes.sfx: Soft pop on the head turn
keyframes.creator_direction: Points off to one side on 'the examiner', away on 'not the subject'. Slight grin.

keyframes.emotion: It cheats, but it mostly fails
keyframes.top_visual: An answer-key icon pops beside the checker with Cut P6 (p.94) behind it. Then nine small attempt dots draw in a row and one fills yellow, with small Cut P7 (p.95). S4 and S5 ghost in beside S3 as faint grey outlines, unlabelled in voice. Grey footer: stronger model → the grader becomes the bottleneck.
keyframes.motion: Key clicks in on 'answer key'; dots draw then one fills on 'one in nine'.
keyframes.creator_direction: Amused, matter of fact; holds up one finger on 'one in nine'.

keyframes.top_visual: S7b: the effort dial draws on the model box with a ₹ needle that ratchets from low to max. Label lands beside it; small grey lines: one coding benchmark · best score at xhigh, not max (p.209). Cut P12 (p.34) small. Dashed tag: MY READ (medium): effort is a trained signal. The dial stays attached to the model box for the next beats.
keyframes.motion: Needle ratchets in four clicks; label stays on through KF16 so it can be read.
keyframes.creator_direction: No speech: eyes flick up to the dial, small 'ouch' wince, back to lens.

keyframes.top_visual: S6: an arc draws over the pipeline with three diamonds appearing in turn. The middle diamond is tagged 'stronger, not released'; the last one drops down and turns green as RELEASED. Cut P8 (p.39, METR's test) and Cut P9 (p.13) slide in small. Dashed tag: MY READ (high): the release is a chosen checkpoint. Grey chip: how the limiting was done: unknown.
keyframes.motion: Arc draws in 0.8 s, diamonds ping in sequence, last diamond drops with a soft bounce.
keyframes.transition_in: Camera tilts up over the pipeline
keyframes.creator_direction: Calm, reassuring tone; small 'set aside' hand gesture on 'wasn't shipped'.

keyframes.top_visual: S7: the model box splits into two lanes labelled Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. A three-step gate (probe → classifier → classifier) draws on the Fable lane with a dashed drop to 'fallback: older Opus'. The effort dial rides onto the Fable lane. Cut P10 (p.78) with highlighter on 'differ only in the safeguards'. Dashed tag: MY READ (high): same underlying model means same weights.
keyframes.motion: Box splits on 'one model'; gate steps click in one by one.
keyframes.creator_direction: Brings both hands together on 'one model'.

keyframes.emotion: Now I see the whole thing (payoff of the paper section)
keyframes.shot: Full-frame: the complete pipeline S0 to S7 pulls back to fill the whole 9:16 frame and holds, with the wrapper gate glowing.
keyframes.top_visual: Blueprint-style pull-back of the whole diagram arranged vertically for the tall frame; everything dims slightly except the gate on the Fable lane. Small Cut P11 (p.47) pinned near the gate. Grey footer: safety is a system property, not only a model property.
keyframes.on_screen_text: THE DIFFERENCE LIVES IN THE WRAPPER
keyframes.motion: 1 s pull-back, then a 1.5 s hold with a gentle glow pulse on the gate.
keyframes.transition_in: Zoom-out from the split panel to full frame
keyframes.creator_direction: Voice only, slower and deliberate on 'lives in the wrapper'.

keyframes.shot: Full-frame section card over the spoken question, about 1.6 s, then the creator finishes the line in split.
keyframes.on_screen_text: WHERE DOES IT EARN THE PRICE?
keyframes.motion: Quick punch-in; 'PRICE' in yellow.
keyframes.music: Brighter lift into the new section

shot_list: 1. Paper cuts (still exports, before the shoot): crop the real PDF pages for P1 p.131, P2 p.11, P3 p.131, P4 p.133, P5 p.95, P6 p.94, P7 p.95, P8 p.39, P9 p.13, P10 p.78, P11 p.47, P12 p.34 and the p.209 effort line. 300 dpi or higher, page number kept in each crop, highlight phrases exactly as in the screenplay.

2. [CLIPS NEEDED] Three Instagram posts of things built with the model, sourced with permission and credit: 9:16 or croppable, 2 s usable each, handle noted for the tag. Screen-record the posts clean, with no app chrome.

3. Screen recording, config/models.yaml: editor in dark theme, font about 20 pt, window cropped to the model-to-job mapping, 4 s captured for about 1.1 s used, static then slow scroll. Check no keys, tokens or private paths are visible.
4. Plate on scale (D4): the original top-down test photo of the 340 g plate with the scale readout legible; if a video of the weigh-in exists, take 3 s. Do not restage with a different plate.
5. Glimpse clip: the existing recording of the Workout Analyser drawing on the lift; pick the clearest 1.5 s, 9:16, for a 1 s use.
6. Creator pick-up, silent reaction for the effort dial: same seated framing, eyes up to the top panel, small wince, back to lens; 3 s, two takes.

7. Creator talking takes in 4K landscape so the edit can crop to the bottom half and punch in to 1.4x (KF09, KF11, KF13, KF28) without softness; neutral lighting and wardrobe so the same M2, M5, M9 to M12 and M14 takes can be graded cold for the trial reel.
8. Optional safety B-roll: 4 to 6 s screen recording of the real Meal Analyser run on that plate (items + grams output), in case the drawn pipeline needs a proof cutaway.
risks: Timing: M6 has 38 spoken words (about 13 s) in a 5 s slot and M7 has no spoken line. I re-timed from 29 s on and gave the dial a 1 s music-only breath, so this cut lands near 90.8 s, about 1 s over the screenplay's estimate. To get under 90 s, drop 'Yet' first as the screenplay says, or draw the dial under 'And the release is curated'.

M11 is the densest stretch: lanes, the A+ sheet, the models.yaml recording and the D7 bars all sit inside about 6.5 s of speech. If it reads as rushed, the D7 inset is the one to move to the comment card.
[CLIPS NEEDED]: the M2 montage has no footage yet. Do not mock up posts or handles; without three real, credited clips the beat needs a different visual.

[DUMMY]: D7 still carries placeholder numbers and a placeholder winner. Keep the stamp visible or swap in real results before publishing; a clean-looking bar chart of dummy data would read as a real result.
S4 and S5 are named but not described in the screenplay I received, so KF14 only ghosts them as outlines; their contents need the pipeline source drawing.

Text load: each paper beat lists a cut, a MY READ tag and an interview line. I kept one hero line of six words or fewer per frame and pushed the rest to small grey footers; even so, KF08, KF14, KF16 and KF17 can clutter on a phone. The interview lines are the first to move to the comment card.

Tips card and Saturday tease are shortened on screen from the screenplay wording to stay readable (the 13-word tease cannot be read in 1 s). Full wording should go on the comment card and in the caption; this needs the creator's approval.
Paper cuts must be real page crops, never re-typed. They say 'Claude Mythos 5.2' while the voice says Fable until M9, which may confuse viewers at KF08 and KF11.

Plate frame: Opus (290 g) is within 5 g of Fable (295 g). Keep the Opus tag neutral so the frame does not imply Fable beat Opus; the claim is only against Haiku, and '34% lower' is portion error, not accuracy.
Effort wording: the p.209 footnote says the best score was at xhigh, while the tip says 'high, not max'. The tips dial must click to HIGH as written; a viewer who pauses may notice the difference.
Tone drift: M5 and M6 (failure mode, cheating) can slide into the trial reel's fear look. Keep coral to small marks, no red wash, no drone, a playful 'uh-oh'.
No logos or brand marks for the model maker or Instagram, no real-looking shop receipts; model names as plain text only.
The full pipeline is unreadable in the half panel, so KF18 must stay full-frame and be laid out vertically.
models.yaml recording: check for secrets and legibility at phone size; never rebuild it as a graphic.
Captions and on-screen text must not stack: when a hero line is on screen, keep the caption to one short line or drop it for that frame.
The screenplay text I received cuts off inside the trial-differences section. The MAIN beats are complete, so this board is unaffected, but the trial board needs the full text.
